title: Three-Body Scattering for Generative Modeling
summary: Modern generative models typically rely on an adversarial critic, a prescribed noise-to-data path, or an autoregressive factorization. Instead, we show that a proper distributional energy can induce sample-level motion and provide direct regression supervision for a one-step generator. Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM) for generation turns the energy distance into a constant-size per-projectile interaction: each projectile is attracted toward one real source and repelled from one independently generated source. Conditioned on the projectile and its condition, its expectation equals the $2$-Wasserstein gradient-flow velocity of $\frac12D_E^2(P_θ,Q)$. A batch of $B$ frozen-target events yields $O(B)$ sample-level losses, each using one reference for its condition instead of the minibatch-wide all-pairs field used by methods such as Drifting Models. Tracking this conditional expectation online can reduce field noise. Using scattering in frozen image features, TBSM trains one-step generators on ImageNet-256, achieving FID${}=2.23$ with pixel-space PixelDiT-XL and FID${}=1.63$ with latent-space DiT-XL at NFE${}=1$. We provide a design map relating diffusion-related supervision, Drift-like dynamics, and GAN-like objectives. These results establish tracked scattering as a route to high-dimensional one-step generation. Code: https://github.com/sp12138/TBSM.
summary_cn: 本论文提出一种基于三体散射动力学的新型生成模型方法。不同于传统的对抗生成网络、扩散模型或自回归方法，该方法通过定义一个合适的分布能量函数，直接驱动样本层面的运动，并为单步生成器提供直接的回归监督信号。这一技术简化了生成模型训练流程，无需对抗训练或复杂的噪声路径设计，有望提升生成效率与稳定性，对AI产品中的快速内容生成、实时交互等场景具有潜在商业价值。
